item.title: About Us
item.description: Our Story Building the Future of Capital Markets We're bridging the gap between blockchain innovation and traditional finance infrastructure, making compliant securities accessible to everyone. Our Mission Traditional capital markets are gatekept by high costs, slow processes, and geographic limitations. Meanwhile, blockchain technology offers unprecedented efficiency but operates in regulatory gray zones. We built Sails.to to solve this paradox — a hybrid infrastructure that delivers the best of both worlds: blockchain's speed and accessibility with traditional finance's legal clarity and institutional trust.

item.title: Accredited Investor - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Compliance Accredited Investor An individual or entity meeting SEC financial thresholds ($200K+ annual income or $1M+ net worth) that qualifies to invest in unregistered securities offerings. Full Definition Under SEC regulations, accredited investors are deemed financially sophisticated enough to understand and bear the risks of unregistered securities. Individuals qualify with annual income exceeding $200,000 ($300,000 joint) for the past two years, or net worth over $1 million excluding primary residence.

item.title: AML (Anti-Money Laundering) - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Compliance AML (Anti-Money Laundering) Laws, regulations, and procedures designed to prevent criminals from disguising illegally obtained funds as legitimate income through financial transactions. Full Definition Anti-Money Laundering encompasses the legal controls and corporate procedures that financial institutions must implement to detect and report suspicious activities. AML programs typically include customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and suspicious activity reporting. Blockchain-based securities platforms integrate AML checks directly into smart contracts to ensure ongoing compliance.

item.title: Cap Table (Capitalization Table) - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Finance Cap Table A complete record of a company's securities ownership, showing all shareholders, their holdings, and ownership percentages, updated in real-time on blockchain. Full Definition A capitalization table tracks who owns what percentage of a company or fund, including all equity classes, convertible instruments, and option pools. Traditional cap tables are maintained in spreadsheets prone to errors. Blockchain-based cap tables update automatically with every token transfer, providing a single source of truth that's always accurate, auditable, and accessible to authorized parties.

item.title: Custody - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Finance Custody The safekeeping and administration of securities on behalf of investors, including settlement, corporate actions processing, and record-keeping. Full Definition Securities custody involves holding assets safely on behalf of clients and handling administrative duties like dividend collection, proxy voting, and corporate action processing. Sails.to offers hybrid custody: tokens can be self-custodied in Solana wallets or held in qualified custody through the ISIN/Clearstream bridge. This flexibility allows investors to choose between DeFi-style control and TradFi-style institutional services.

item.title: Distributions - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Finance Distributions Payments made to security token holders, including dividends, interest, rental income, or liquidation proceeds, automated via smart contracts. Full Definition Distributions are payments from issuers to token holders, representing their share of profits, income, or proceeds. On Sails.to, distributions are automated through smart contracts: when an issuer initiates a distribution, the system calculates each holder's share based on the real-time cap table and executes payments directly to their wallets (or traditional accounts for ISIN holders).

item.title: Professional Investor - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Compliance Professional Investor Under EU/international regulations, an investor with sufficient experience, knowledge, and expertise to make independent investment decisions and assess risks. Full Definition Professional investors, as defined by MiFID II and similar international frameworks, include institutional investors (banks, funds, pension schemes), large corporations meeting asset/turnover thresholds, and individuals who opt-in based on qualitative criteria (transaction frequency, portfolio size, professional experience). Many security token offerings outside the US are structured for professional investors only to reduce regulatory burden.

item.title: Regulation D (Reg D) - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Compliance Regulation D (Reg D) SEC regulation providing exemptions from registration for private placements, allowing companies to raise capital from accredited investors without a public offering. Full Definition Regulation D provides three exemption rules (504, 506(b), and 506(c)) for private securities offerings. Rule 506(b) allows unlimited capital raises from up to 35 non-accredited investors (with restrictions) and unlimited accredited investors, but prohibits general solicitation. Rule 506(c) permits general solicitation but requires all investors to be verified accredited investors.

item.title: Regulation S (Reg S) - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Compliance Regulation S (Reg S) SEC regulation providing a safe harbor for securities offerings made outside the United States to non-US persons, exempt from SEC registration requirements. Full Definition Regulation S establishes safe harbors from SEC registration for offerings conducted entirely outside the US. To qualify, offers and sales must occur in offshore transactions with no directed selling efforts in the US. Reg S is commonly combined with Reg D offerings, allowing issuers to sell to accredited US investors under Reg D while simultaneously offering to international investors under Reg S.

item.title: Secondary Trading - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Finance Secondary Trading The buying and selling of securities after their initial issuance, providing liquidity and price discovery for investors seeking to exit positions. Full Definition Secondary trading occurs when investors trade previously issued securities among themselves, rather than buying directly from the issuer. For tokenized securities, secondary markets can operate 24/7 on blockchain-based exchanges, with smart contracts automatically enforcing transfer restrictions and compliance. Sails.to's broker network facilitates compliant secondary trading, matching buyers with sellers while ensuring all parties meet eligibility requirements.

item.title: Security Token - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Finance Security Token A digital representation of a traditional security (equity, debt, or fund share) issued on a blockchain with built-in compliance rules enforced by smart contracts. Full Definition Security tokens are blockchain-based digital assets that represent ownership in real-world securities such as company shares, bonds, real estate, or fund interests. Unlike utility tokens, security tokens are subject to securities regulations and must comply with laws like Reg D, Reg S, or Reg A+ in the US.

item.title: Series LLC - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Legal Series LLC A corporate structure allowing a single LLC to create multiple segregated series, each with its own assets, liabilities, and members, providing liability isolation between series. Full Definition A Series LLC is a unique business structure that allows the creation of separate "series" under one master LLC umbrella. Each series operates as a distinct entity with its own assets, liabilities, contracts, and even members, while sharing administrative overhead.

item.title: Smart Contract - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Technology Smart Contract Self-executing code deployed on a blockchain that automatically enforces the terms of an agreement when predetermined conditions are met. Full Definition Smart contracts are programs stored on a blockchain that run when triggered by transactions meeting specific conditions. For security tokens, smart contracts encode compliance rules (investor eligibility, transfer restrictions, holding periods), automate corporate actions (dividends, voting), and maintain the cap table. Once deployed, the rules execute automatically without intermediaries, providing transparency and reducing operational costs.

item.title: Solana - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Technology Solana A high-performance blockchain platform known for fast transaction speeds (400ms finality) and low fees, used by Sails.to for issuing security tokens. Full Definition Solana is a Layer 1 blockchain designed for speed and scalability, capable of processing thousands of transactions per second with sub-second finality. Its low transaction costs (fractions of a cent) and fast confirmation times make it well-suited for security token operations that require frequent on-chain actions like dividend distributions, cap table updates, and compliance checks.

item.title: SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Legal SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) A subsidiary entity created for a specific, limited purpose, typically to isolate financial risk and hold specific assets separate from a parent company. Full Definition A Special Purpose Vehicle (also called Special Purpose Entity) is a legal entity created to fulfill a narrow, specific objective—usually to isolate assets and liabilities for financing, risk management, or regulatory purposes. In tokenized securities, SPVs are commonly used to hold underlying assets (real estate, company shares, etc.

item.title: Tokenization - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Finance Tokenization The process of converting ownership rights in an asset into digital tokens on a blockchain, enabling fractional ownership and programmable compliance. Full Definition Tokenization transforms traditional assets—real estate, company equity, art, funds—into digital tokens representing fractional ownership shares. Each token is backed by the underlying asset and carries legal rights (dividends, voting, proceeds). Blockchain tokenization enables 24/7 trading, instant settlement, fractional ownership in small denominations, automated compliance, and global accessibility while maintaining regulatory compliance.

item.title: TradFi Bridge - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Finance TradFi Bridge Sails.to's mechanism for converting blockchain-native security tokens to traditional ISIN securities that can be held in conventional bank custody. Full Definition The TradFi (Traditional Finance) Bridge is a unique feature of Sails.to that allows investors to move between blockchain and traditional custody. Tokens held on Solana can be "bridged" to receive an ISIN and be settled through Clearstream, appearing in the investor's regular brokerage account.

item.title: Wyoming DAO LLC - Glossary
item.description: ← Back to Glossary Legal Wyoming DAO LLC A limited liability company structure recognized by Wyoming law that allows decentralized autonomous organizations to operate with legal entity status and liability protection. Full Definition Wyoming became the first US state to legally recognize DAOs as a distinct business entity type in 2021. A Wyoming DAO LLC combines the flexibility of smart contract governance with the legal protections of a traditional LLC, including limited liability for members.
